description: Observed-order-of-accuracy sweep for grids/latlon3d/rules/ppm_D_lat_zero_grad_bc (Piecewise Parabolic Method, Colella-Woodward 1984, semi-discrete method-of-lines flux, zero-gradient pole ghosts) driven by problems/latlon3d_advection_meridional_ppm.esm — the rank-3 meridional analogue of the 1-D bounded sibling advection_1d_inflow_ppm, with passive lon (NLON=8) and lev (NLEV=4) axes. The problem is loaded once per resolution with the loader-API metaparameter binding (esm-spec 9.7.6 binding site 4): NLAT is the open metaparameter; dlat_deg = 180/(NLAT-1) follows each rebinding. Manufactured steady u*(lat)=cos^4((pi/180)lat); the t=0.2 drift is the operator truncation. HONEST ORDER: PPM is nominally 3rd order and the unlimited interior flux-difference is exactly the 4th-order central first derivative, but the global order is set by the one-sided PPM boundary reconstruction at the poles (and the CW84 limiter can clip the equatorial smooth maximum), so it is sub-nominal. The Julia golden gives median observed order 2.00 in L2 (pairwise 2.00, 1.93, 2.01) but only 1.68 in Linf (pairwise 1.42, 1.68, 2.18): u*=cos^4 has an interior MAXIMUM at the equator, which the CW84 limiter clips (flattening the parabola there), so the pointwise Linf order lags the L2 order (unlike the monotone-profile 1-D bounded sibling advection_1d_inflow_ppm, whose cos(pi x) has no interior extremum and stays near 2 in both norms). expected_order 1.85 with order_tolerance 0.25 brackets BOTH norm medians honestly (deviation 0.15 in L2, 0.17 in Linf). NOT a claim of 3rd order.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator

blocked_upstream_bindings.rust: Same CW84-limited PPM RHS (stencils/ppm_flux -> ppm_limit_right, a large non-smooth min/max ifelse AST) that hangs earthsci-ast-rs's diffsol integrator on the other PPM sweeps (advection_1d_ppm_periodic, advection_1d_inflow_ppm, latlon3d_advection_zonal_ppm): diffsol has no dtmin/max-step fail-fast guard, so it drives dt->0 without terminating instead of erroring. Julia (Tsit5) and Python (LSODA) solve it. Remove once the Rust solver gains a step guard.
